stories.title: Maruti Suzuki dominates October sales
stories.summary: Maruti Suzuki models took seven of the top ten spots in October 2026. The Wagon R led with 23,747 units, a 25 percent increase year-on-year, while the Brezza climbed to second place with 22,436 units. The Tata Nexon fell to third. Growth is apparently a matter of volume.

stories.title: Tata Motors maintains lead over Mahindra in EV push
stories.summary: Tata Motors has maintained its lead over Mahindra in the passenger vehicle market for most of fiscal year 2027, with a cumulative lead of 28,124 vehicles. Electric vehicles remain a key differentiator, with Tata registering 88,125 units compared to Mahindra's 50,322 during the April to October period.

stories.title: Commercial vehicle retail sales reach October record
stories.summary: Retail sales for commercial vehicles hit 115,140 units in October, marking the highest-ever total for the month. While medium and heavy vehicle sales grew by over 20 percent, light commercial vehicle sales declined by 9.57 percent year-on-year. The segment continues to show contrasting performance trends.

stories.title: Mercedes-Benz targets 20 percent EV sales in India
stories.summary: Chairman Ola Källenius expects electric vehicles to account for more than one in five Mercedes-Benz sales in India by 2027. The company aims to move from a high-single-digit share in 2026 to double digits next year. The forecast is not a commitment to stop selling combustion engines.

stories.title: Ola Källenius says India is central to Mercedes-Benz
stories.summary: Mercedes-Benz Chairman Ola Källenius stated that the company's Indian operations are increasingly vital to its global business, citing component sourcing and engineering. Källenius noted that he cannot imagine a Mercedes being developed without Indian involvement. The company has not yet decided to export complete vehicles from India.

stories.title: Rohan Chowta promoted at Škoda India
stories.summary: Rohan Chowta has been appointed head of product and sales planning at Škoda India. A veteran of Volkswagen India, Chowta joined the company in September 2025 as lead sales planning. His new mandate involves deciding what to sell and working out how to sell it.

stories.title: States clash over ethanol blending in petrol
stories.summary: Karnataka has defended findings of excessive ethanol content in fuel samples, while Kerala has begun independent testing. The dispute concerns India's E20 standard, which permits up to 20 percent ethanol blending. Authorities are questioning fuel quality, vehicle compatibility, and consumer protection.

stories.summary: Glovis America is expanding its operations at Port Tampa Bay, adding 32 acres to its existing terminal. stories.title: Ashok Leyland unifies commercial vehicle portfolios
stories.summary: Ashok Leyland has consolidated its medium, heavy and light commercial vehicle verticals under Chief Marketing Officer Sanjeev Kumar. stories.title: Turkish automotive logistics faces export strain
stories.summary: Türkiye remains a major automotive manufacturing hub for Europe, but falling export volumes and shifting production patterns are testing its logistics network. A new whitepaper notes that while 87 percent of exports head to the European Union, the infrastructure is currently under growing strain.

stories.title: Autonomous shuttle trials begin at Portsmouth port
stories.summary: Aurrigo International is trialing its Auto-Shuttle electric vehicle at Portsmouth International Port. The project, backed by the Freight Innovation Fund, aims to transport people and freight on a 1km route to demonstrate that driverless technology can operate safely within a live, mixed-traffic port environment.

stories.title: Worldpac to open automated Georgia distribution center
stories.summary: Automotive parts distributor Worldpac plans to open a 413,000-square-foot automated distribution center in Forest Park, Georgia, in the first half of 2027. The facility is expected to create over 150 jobs and serve customers across the Southeast region.

stories.summary: The global plating on plastics market is navigating a landscape shaped by supply chain realignments and regulatory pressures on heavy metals. According to an IndexBox report, the sector enters 2026 with more disciplined procurement behavior and a focus on enhancing the value of engineered plastic components.

stories.title: Plastics and rubber machinery market shifts to automation
stories.summary: The global plastics and rubber machinery market is shifting capital investment from capacity expansion toward modernization and sustainability compliance. An IndexBox report notes that the industry is entering a structurally distinct phase, prioritizing automation as it replaces aging equipment in mature economies.

stories.title: Snap rings market enters 2026
stories.summary: The global snap rings market enters 2026 with what IndexBox describes as broader demand fundamentals and a more regionally diversified supply architecture. The components are deeply integrated into mechanical assemblies across automotive, aerospace, and consumer electronics. The market remains a critical, if often overlooked, industrial component.

stories.title: Lacquer spray equipment market shifts
stories.summary: The global market for lacquer spray equipment enters 2026 with what IndexBox calls more disciplined procurement behavior. The sector is undergoing a structural transformation driven by environmental regulations and material science advancements. The equipment is described as a critical enabler of finish quality and material utilization.

stories.title: Auto retail sales fall in October
stories.summary: Retail auto sales in India declined 24 percent in October, according to Gaadiwaadi.com. Despite the overall monthly downturn, the festival of Dhanteras provided a temporary boost to vehicle deliveries. Further details were thin in the open report.

stories.title: Dealer margins remain thin despite EV growth
stories.summary: Indian auto dealers are facing low margins on electric vehicles despite an 11.5 percent market penetration in October. The Federation of Automobile Dealers Associations notes that investments in infrastructure, specialized workshops, and skilled technicians are increasing operating costs as sales reach 3.55 lakh units.

stories.title: Cox Automotive updates Xtime scheduler
stories.summary: Cox Automotive has launched an enhanced Xtime consumer scheduling portal. The company says the update simplifies appointment booking across desktop and mobile devices. The modernized interface aims to reduce clicks and provide clearer views of pricing and promotions for service customers.

stories.title: Hendrick Automotive Group adds call training
stories.summary: Hendrick Automotive Group has partnered with RockED to launch an inbound sales call certification program for its staff. The 90-minute annual training is designed to build conversation skills for employees across its 100 dealerships. The company says the program has improved appointment and show rates.

stories.title: Hertz to close physical car sales stores
stories.summary: Hertz will close all physical Hertz Car Sales locations to focus on its online retail strategy. The company says it is expanding its online buying platform and growing its TestDrive+ program at rental sites. The rental network is now the primary channel for retail sales.

stories.title: Mexico updates antitrust framework for auto dealers
stories.summary: Mexico is modernizing its competition framework, shifting enforcement from the COFECE apparatus to the National Competition Authority. As vehicle sales approach record volumes, automotive manufacturers face increased vertical liability and stricter corporate oversight regarding dealer franchise agreements under the Federal Economic Competition Law.

stories.title: Ford sues aftermarket parts distributor
stories.summary: Ford has filed a design patent infringement lawsuit against Empire Auto Parts in a Dallas federal court. The complaint alleges unauthorized use of patents covering grilles, fenders, hoods, and lighting components. Ford is seeking an injunction and monetary relief for the identified catalogue items.

stories.title: Penske Automotive Group merger under investigation
stories.summary: Penske Automotive Group is facing an investigation into its pending take-private merger. The deal involves controlling shareholders Roger Penske and Mitsui and Co. taking the company private. The full details of the investigation are for subscribers.

stories.title: Used car dealer faces court charges
stories.summary: Blackbrook Car Sales Company Ltd has appeared in court facing seven charges under the Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024. stories.title: Hyundai launches usage-based insurance in India
stories.summary: Hyundai Motor India has introduced a usage-based insurance program for connected vehicles. The initiative generates a driving score based on data from the Bluelink platform, which may qualify responsible drivers for insurance renewal benefits. The program was announced on November 5.

stories.title: Court rejects malpractice claim over divorce error
stories.summary: An Arizona appeals court has ruled that a woman cannot receive compensation from her former lawyer after a missed deadline prevented the correction of a $100,000 error in her divorce decree. The court found no proof that the mistake caused direct financial loss.

stories.title: Bank loses bid to recover loan guarantee
stories.summary: A Texas appeals court has upheld a ruling that prevents PlainsCapital Bank from recovering a $29 million loan guarantee. The loan was tied to a fuel investment venture later exposed as a Ponzi scheme. The court found the bank failed to prove its case.

stories.title: Government expected to weaken electric vehicle sales targets
stories.summary: The Government is expected to weaken manufacturer targets for new electric vehicle sales this week. The current mandate requires 80 percent of new car sales to be fully electric by 2030, with a 100 percent target by 2035. The Department for Transport launched a review of the mandate in August.

stories.title: Government weighs reducing 2030 electric car target to 60 percent
stories.summary: Ministers are concluding a review of the zero-emission vehicle mandate, with reports suggesting the Government may reduce the 2030 electric car sales target from 80 percent to 60 percent. Andy Burnham has insisted no final decision has been made on the potential retreat from the policy.

stories.title: PRI and SEMA release 2027 advocacy agenda
stories.summary: PRI and SEMA have released their 2027 Advocacy Agenda at the 2026 SEMA Show in Las Vegas. The agenda serves as a reference point for the automotive aftermarket industry, outlining federal and state issues that impact the nation's enthusiasts and the industry's members.

stories.title: India faces $6.5 trillion gap in net-zero transition
stories.summary: A report by economist Nicki Hutley suggests India’s 2070 net-zero target could require $22.7 trillion in investment. While domestic resources may cover 70 percent of requirements, the country faces an estimated $6.5 trillion financing gap. International capital is described as crucial to achieving these climate goals.

stories.title: India launches first hydrogen-powered train
stories.summary: Indian Railways inaugurated its first indigenous hydrogen-powered train on 17 July 2026. The locomotive generates electricity onboard using hydrogen fuel cell technology. The train is set to begin operations on the Jind-Sonipat section of the Northern Railway to advance green rail mobility.

stories.title: RecyClass confirms recyclability of automotive polypropylene
stories.summary: RecyClass has confirmed that impact-modified polypropylene compounds used in automotive bumpers are compatible with mechanical recycling streams in Europe. The testing campaign assessed nine industrial formulations to provide evidence for the development of closed-loop recycling systems in the automotive and electrical sectors.

stories.title: Volkswagen to dismantle vehicles for spare parts in Zwickau
stories.summary: Volkswagen is opening an industrial dismantling line at its electric vehicle factory in Zwickau to recover parts for older cars. Starting in 2027, the line is scheduled to process 4,100 vehicles per year. The project will employ 100 workers who have been retrained for the assignment.

stories.title: National Bank of Malawi buys electric vehicle
stories.summary: National Bank of Malawi has purchased an electric vehicle for K74 million to promote green financing and embed environmental, social and governance principles. SME Consultant Micheal Chikapa said the car represents a milestone in the bank's ambition to lead the country's shift to a greener economy.

stories.title: China car exports rise as domestic sales contract
stories.summary: China saw passenger vehicle exports rise 68.2 percent to 932,000 units in October, while domestic sales fell 27.3 percent to 1.65 million cars. This marks a twelfth consecutive month of domestic contraction, pushing automakers to expand further into overseas markets to find buyers.

stories.title: China expects slower export growth in 2027
stories.summary: The China Passenger Car Association expects export growth to slow to 10 percent in 2027, down from the supercharged pace of 2026. Secretary general Cui Dongshu attributed the expected cooling to international markets introducing higher tariffs and import quotas to protect their own local industries.

stories.title: General Motors to shift production from Mexico to US
stories.summary: General Motors will invest US$4 billion to expand production in Michigan, Kansas and Tennessee. The company plans to reallocate assembly of the Chevrolet Blazer and Equinox from Mexico to the U.S. starting in 2027. Operations in Mexico will continue with current personnel levels intact.
